'''''Lithocarpus edulis''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family ''[[Fagaceae]]''.<ref name=POWO>{{cite web |url= https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:358737-1 |title= Lithocarpus edulis (Makino) Nakai |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=July 27, 2025}}</ref><ref name=COL>{{cite web |url= https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/6QKYG |title= Lithocarpus edulis (Makino) Nakai |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Catalogue of Life |publisher=Species 2000 |access-date=July 27, 2025}}</ref> It is sometimes referred to by the common name '''Japanese stone oak''' and is native to [[Japan]] and the [[Ryukyu Islands]].<ref name=POWO/> It is an [[evergreen]] [[tree]] growing up to 15 metres tall. The nuts are edible for people but taste bitter. The nuts contain [[tannin]]s, however soaking them in water removes them. It is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]].
